comments.author: Akhil Mathew
comments.html: It’s actually not quite true that the *higher* algebraic K-theory of the ring of C^\infty functions on a compact manifold M (or continuous functions on a compact space) is the topological K-theory of M; for instance, if M is a point, then the algebraic K-theory of the complex numbers is not quite KU. (However, it is KU up to p-adic completion at any prime p.) In the construction of topological K-theory, it is important that the topology on the real or complex numbers should be taken into account. You might be interested in the paper http://arxiv.org/pdf/1110.5851v2.pdf where these distinctions are important (although the algebraic version is used).
